# Neba

> Neba is a React UI component library published to npm as `neba`. Behaviour and accessibility come from [Base UI](https://base-ui.com) primitives; styling comes from [Tailwind CSS](https://tailwindcss.com) v4. It ships as ESM only with type declarations included, has two runtime dependencies (`@base-ui/react`, and `highlight.js` which only CodeBlock reaches and only through a dynamic import), and supports dark mode out of the box.

The design language: **a Neba surface is a sheet of cut acrylic, not a moulded plastic key.** A control never moves — there is no `transform` on press — it answers in colour and depth instead. Press is instant and release is slow. `elevation` defaults to `0`, and `0` means no shadow at all; the acrylic edge is what separates a surface from the page.

Every component draws from one shared prop vocabulary, so `size="md"` means the same thing everywhere:

```ts
type NebaSize = 'xs' | 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg' | 'xl';
type NebaColor = 'primary' | 'secondary' | 'success' | 'warning' | 'danger' | 'info';
type NebaDensity = 'default' | 'compact';
type NebaVariant = 'solid' | 'outline' | 'text';
type NebaElevation = 0 | 1 | 2 | 3;
```

`color` is one of six semantic families, never an arbitrary value like `#4072cd`. Setup is `npm install neba`, then one line in the app's CSS entry point — `@import 'neba/styles.css';`. That file ships compiled, so Tailwind is not a requirement on the consumer's side. A project that already runs Tailwind v4 imports `neba/tailwind.css` instead, which is the token sheet and registers the package as a Tailwind source, so consumers never write an `@source` of their own.

Documentation is available in English (served from `/`) and Korean (served from `/ko/`). The links below are the English pages; prefix any path with `/ko` for the Korean version.

## Guide

- [Getting started](https://neba.cdget.com/guide/getting-started): Install, the one-line CSS setup, what the bundled reset does, the Tailwind path, first component, Next.js and React Server Components, dark mode via `data-theme` or a class, browser support.
- [Hooks](https://neba.cdget.com/guide/hooks): The hooks the components already run on, offered from `neba/hooks` — `useDisclosure` for the `open`/`onOpenChange` pair every overlay takes, `useMediaQuery` and `useBreakpoint` over one live `MediaQueryList` per query for the whole page, `useCurrentBreakpoint` and `useBreakpointValue` for reading a per-breakpoint map in JavaScript exactly as the CSS cascade reads it, `usePrefersReducedMotion` for the motion written in JavaScript rather than in a keyframe, `useElementSize` and `useOnScreen` over one shared observer each, and `useShortcut` for a key combination bound on the window in the same spelling `Shortcut` draws. There is deliberately no general-purpose hook collection: everything here is machinery the library needed for itself.
- [NebaProvider](https://neba.cdget.com/guide/provider): One optional place to set what every component under it starts from. `defaults` fills in `size`, `density`, `variant` and `locale` — four axes whose right value is a property of the product rather than of a control — with the call site still winning; `color` and `elevation` are deliberately excluded, because a component's colour default is often semantic and a shadow is opt-in per surface. The colour scheme writes `data-theme` **and** `color-scheme` on `<html>` (the second is what turns the browser's own scrollbars and form controls over), remembers the choice, and is read with `useColorScheme()`, where `colorScheme` keeps `system` as its own answer and `resolvedColorScheme` never is. `colorSchemeScript()` is the inline `<head>` script that stops the first-paint flash, sharing the provider's key and attribute. `direction` sets `dir` and wraps Base UI's DirectionProvider, and is left alone when not given.
- [Design language](https://neba.cdget.com/design/design-language): The cut-acrylic rule and everything that follows from it — the four surface layers, the no-transform rule, instant press and slow release, the elevation ladder, translucency and blur.
- [Colour](https://neba.cdget.com/design/color): The six semantic families, the five hand-picked tokens per family, and how everything else is derived with `color-mix()`. Includes a live palette table read back from the browser.
- [Breakpoints](https://neba.cdget.com/design/breakpoints): The five widths (`xs` 0, `sm` 40rem, `md` 48rem, `lg` 64rem, `xl` 80rem — Tailwind's own), the rule that every entry in a per-breakpoint map is a floor and narrows rather than replaces, which props are responsive and why the class-valued axes are not, when to decide in CSS (`Show`) versus in JavaScript (`useBreakpoint`), and how to move the widths: a `@theme` override on the Tailwind path, since `@media` cannot read a custom property and a breakpoint is therefore a build-time decision.
- [Prop conventions](https://neba.cdget.com/design/prop-conventions): What the shared props mean, which components take which axes, and the rule against inventing a second spelling for an idea that already has one.

## Components

- [All components](https://neba.cdget.com/components/): Every released component on one page, each card a running preview rather than a picture.

### Inputs

- [Button](https://neba.cdget.com/components/inputs/button): A control that runs an action. Base UI's Button primitive with Neba's acrylic surface on top.
- [ButtonGroup](https://neba.cdget.com/components/inputs/button-group): A row of buttons that belong together; corners facing a neighbour are squared off and shared props are set once for the whole set.
- [TextField](https://neba.cdget.com/components/inputs/text-field): Single- or multi-line text input. Label, description and error are one component, wired together by Base UI's Field.
- [Select](https://neba.cdget.com/components/inputs/select): One value chosen from a list. The trigger is a TextField's shell wearing a chevron.
- [Checkbox](https://neba.cdget.com/components/inputs/checkbox): A single yes/no, or one member of a set.
- [RadioGroup](https://neba.cdget.com/components/inputs/radio-group): A set of options where exactly one is chosen.
- [Switch](https://neba.cdget.com/components/inputs/switch): An immediate on/off. The difference from a Checkbox is temporal, not visual.
- [Slider](https://neba.cdget.com/components/inputs/slider): A value chosen along a range. Pass an array and it becomes a range slider.
- [Menu](https://neba.cdget.com/components/inputs/menu): A list of actions that appears when something is pressed. Nests, holds state, fully keyboard-driven.
- [FilePicker](https://neba.cdget.com/components/inputs/file-picker): A dashed box you drop files on, or press to open the file dialog.
- [Pagination](https://neba.cdget.com/components/inputs/pagination): A row of page numbers, every one of them a real Button.
- [Combobox](https://neba.cdget.com/components/inputs/combobox): A field you can type into and also choose from; the text filters the list and can become the value itself.
- [TreeSelect](https://neba.cdget.com/components/inputs/tree-select): A value chosen from a tree rather than from a list — a category, a folder, a region, an org-chart node. `selectableBranches` is off by default and that default carries weight: in most of these trees the branches are the taxonomy and the leaves are the answers, so a "Europe" choosable alongside "France" is a data model nobody meant; an item's own `selectable` overrides it either way. `searchable` filters the tree and **keeps every ancestor of a match**, opening the branches it kept — a tree filtered to bare matches is a list, which is what the tree was chosen over, and a match folded inside a closed parent was not shown. `multiple` holds any number and `format` decides how the trigger writes them.
- [NumberField](https://neba.cdget.com/components/inputs/number-field): A field that only holds a number — a TextField's shell plus stepping, clamping and formatting.
- [IconButton](https://neba.cdget.com/components/inputs/icon-button): A round button with a glyph in it and nothing else. Everything else is Button's, and `label` is required rather than optional.
- [Calendar](https://neba.cdget.com/components/inputs/calendar): The same grid the four pickers open, inline and with no popup around it — for a page where the dates are always visible. `mode` decides the value: one `Date`, an array of them, or a `{ start, end }` span. In multiple mode a second click on a held day takes it back out; in range mode a click below the start begins a new span rather than inverting the old one, because inverting is what makes a reader believe they mis-clicked. `renderDay` puts a dot, a count or a bar under a number. It is deliberately **not** a scheduler: the cells are the control ladder's heights, so there is no room for a day's worth of entries and a component that drew those would need a different grid.
- [DatePicker](https://neba.cdget.com/components/inputs/date-picker): One day, chosen from a calendar. The month name and the year are each a button that opens a grid of its own, so any month is two clicks away and any year is three. `granularity` makes one of those grids the answer, for a picker that asks for a whole month or a whole year.
- [TimePicker](https://neba.cdget.com/components/inputs/time-picker): A time of day, chosen from columns. Bounds are checked against the span a row stands for, which is what keeps half past nine reachable when the minimum is 09:30.
- [DateTimePicker](https://neba.cdget.com/components/inputs/date-time-picker): A day and a time in one popup, with the calendar and the clock at the same height and `minDate` read at full precision.
- [DateRangePicker](https://neba.cdget.com/components/inputs/date-range-picker): A span between two days. Two months side by side, a band drawn as the pointer moves, and named presets beside them.
- [SegmentedButton](https://neba.cdget.com/components/inputs/segmented-button): Two or more choices in one pill, exactly one of them taken. A radio group underneath, with a tile that slides between the segments and transforms nothing.
- [OtpField](https://neba.cdget.com/components/inputs/otp-field): A row of one-character slots for a short code typed in from somewhere else — a PIN, a texted verification code, an invite key. `charset` decides what is accepted, `groupSize` where the gaps fall.
- [ColorPicker](https://neba.cdget.com/components/inputs/color-picker): A colour chosen by eye — a saturation square, a hue rail, an optional opacity rail, a field to type a value into and a grid of swatches. Reads and writes hex, `rgb()` and `hsl()`, with no colour library underneath.
- [Rating](https://neba.cdget.com/components/inputs/rating): A score, as a row of stars. Choosable it is a radio group of real `<input>`s — one tab stop, arrow keys, a value in a form submission; `readOnly` it is a single `role="img"` reporting an average, and the one read-only in the library that keeps its colour. `precision` bounds what can be picked without rounding what is displayed.
- [BottomNavigation](https://neba.cdget.com/components/inputs/bottom-navigation): A bar of an app's main destinations, fixed to the bottom edge of the window. A `<nav>` of ordinary buttons or links with `aria-current` on the one you are on, rather than a tab list it would not honour. `labels` decides which names are drawn; an undrawn one is still read out. `safeArea` clears a phone's home indicator.
- [FloatingBottomNavigation](https://neba.cdget.com/components/inputs/floating-bottom-navigation): The same destinations as a BottomNavigation, floating clear of the bottom edge instead of attached to it — a stadium only as wide as what is in it, with the page carrying on underneath. `offset` is the gap it floats above, `labels` defaults to `selected` because a bar sized by its contents cannot afford five drawn names, and `position` adds `absolute` for a bar that belongs to a region rather than the window. It takes the same `BottomNavigationItem` children.
- [FloatingActionButton](https://neba.cdget.com/components/inputs/floating-action-button): The one action a screen is about, floating over it — a FAB. `extended` writes the label beside the glyph; `corner`, `offset` and `position` decide where it sits, including inside a region rather than the window. Given FloatingAction children it becomes a dial that fans out, closes on Escape and returns the focus.
- [CommandPalette](https://neba.cdget.com/components/inputs/command-palette): Everything an application can do, behind one field — the shape a keyboard-first product takes once it has more actions than a menu bar can hold. Not a Menu (a short list, all of it visible before you look) and not a Combobox (what comes back is not a value, it is something happening). `keywords` are words the query matches but that are never drawn, which is what makes `undo` find `Roll back`; `group` draws a heading each time it changes; `shortcut` binds the opening keystroke on the window, `Mod` resolving per platform, and `false` binds nothing.
- [Transfer](https://neba.cdget.com/components/inputs/transfer): Two lists and the arrows between them — everything that could be chosen on one side, everything that has been on the other. For a choice long enough that a Combobox full of chips stops being readable. `value` is what is on the right, in the order `items` gives, so a row does not move when it is sent across and back; ticking a row is not choosing it — ticks say what the next press moves. `searchable` filters a list without moving anything, and a hidden row is not part of a press.
- [NavigationMenu](https://neba.cdget.com/components/inputs/navigation-menu): A site's navigation — a row of destinations, some of which open a panel of more of them. The difference from a Menu is what the rows *are*: a menu holds actions, so its rows are `menuitem`s; this holds links, so it is a `<nav>` full of real `<a>`s, which is what puts them in the link list, on the status bar and in a crawler's index. An item with children is a trigger and a panel, one with an `href` and nothing else is a link. `columns` lays a wide panel out in two or three; one panel is open at a time and it resizes between items rather than closing and reopening.
- [Menubar](https://neba.cdget.com/components/inputs/menubar): The strip of words at the top of an application — File, Edit, View — each opening a menu. What makes it a bar rather than a row of separate menus is what happens once one is open: moving along the strip walks through the others instead of closing the one you left. `MenubarMenu` takes a `label` and the same rows a Menu does; `size`, `color` and `density` belong to the bar. It draws no surface, because a menu bar sits *on* something — a Toolbar, a WindowPane's title bar, a Header.
- [Form](https://neba.cdget.com/components/inputs/form): A `<form>` that knows which of its fields is wrong. A submit collects every field's validity at once and focuses the first that failed; `errors` — keyed by each field's `name` — puts a server's answer back on the field it belongs to rather than in a banner, and clears it as soon as that field changes. `validationMode` is `onSubmit` by default, which is the only setting that does not tell somebody their email is wrong while they are still typing it. Not a form library: no schema, no resolver, no field array — `errors` is the seam those hand off to.
- [Fieldset](https://neba.cdget.com/components/inputs/fieldset): A group of controls that answer one question together, with a name on it. It draws no surface, because a grouping is not a sheet — put it in a Card when one is wanted. `legend` becomes the accessible name of every control inside, so it is written as a phrase rather than a question, and `disabled` reaches every control in it, including ones a component three levels down rendered.
- [Toggle](https://neba.cdget.com/components/inputs/toggle): A button that stays down — it holds a state rather than running an action. `variant` says how it looks while it is *off*; on is always the colour family asserting itself, so an unpressed toggle never reads as pressed. With no label it goes square around its icon, which is the shape a toolbar wants.
- [ToggleGroup](https://neba.cdget.com/components/inputs/toggle-group): A set of toggles that share one state. The corners facing a neighbour are squared off the way a ButtonGroup's are, the value is an array in both the single and the multiple case, and `variant`, `size`, `color`, `density`, `elevation` and `disabled` are set once for the set. One tab stop, arrow keys between the members.

### Display

- [Typography](https://neba.cdget.com/components/display/typography): The library's type scale on its own.
- [VisuallyHidden](https://neba.cdget.com/components/display/visually-hidden): Content that is in the accessibility tree and not on the screen — the word behind an icon button's glyph, the count behind a dot, a caption a table is described by. A 1px clipped box, which is the one form that works: `display: none` takes the text off the tree with the screen, `opacity: 0` leaves a clickable ghost the size of the words, and `text-indent: -9999px` makes a box that wide. `visible` takes the hiding off, which is what a skip link needs once it has the focus; `render` swaps the span for a div, an anchor or a caption. It is the other half of `aria-hidden`, which stays an attribute because it belongs on an element that is already being drawn.
- [Divider](https://neba.cdget.com/components/display/divider): A rule between two things. Not a surface — no acrylic, no light, no shadow.
- [Chip](https://neba.cdget.com/components/display/chip): A compact token — a tag, a filter, a status, an entity plucked out of a list.
- [CodeBlock](https://neba.cdget.com/components/display/code-block): A viewer for one line of code or a thousand. Syntax highlighting is highlight.js reached through a dynamic import, so the grammars are their own chunk and a block that does not colour anything fetches none of them; thirty-four languages come with it and `registerLanguage` teaches it any other. Every part of the chrome is a prop — `toolbar`, `showLanguage`, `copyable`, `rawToggle`, `lineNumbers`, `startLine`. `theme` is `dark` by default and does not follow the page unless it is set to `auto`; there are twelve — four of the library's own (`dark`, `light`, `auto`, `mono`) and eight ports (`one-dark`, `dracula`, `monokai`, `nord`, `night-owl`, `gruvbox`, `github`, `solarized-light`) — and the prop takes any string, because a theme is a set of `--n-code-*` custom properties under a `[data-code-theme]` selector and nothing else. `highlightLines` marks lines with a tinted row: a number, a string of lines and ranges (`'1,4-9,12'`), or an array of either. A `prompt` symbol is generated content, so it cannot be selected, found or copied. Ctrl/Cmd+A inside the focused block selects the code and nothing else.
- [DataTable](https://neba.cdget.com/components/display/data-table): A table for tens of thousands of rows: only the ones on screen are in the DOM, and it sorts, searches, pages and selects them. `height` is what turns virtual scrolling on. Selection follows the file manager — click, Ctrl-click, Shift-click, click-and-drag, and the arrow keys with the same modifiers — with `checkboxes` as an option rather than the default. Headings sort (single or multi-key) and drag wider; adjacent columns sharing a `group` merge into a second header row; `paging="pages"` swaps the scroll for a footer with a page-size Select and a Pagination. `manual` hands any of sort, filter and paging back to the caller for a table whose rows come from a server. Columns can be **pinned** to either edge (which also moves them there, since a frozen column between scrolling ones slides over its neighbours), **reordered** through `columnOrder` — where a key the list does not name keeps its place, so a column added later does not vanish out of a stored order — and dragged when `reorderable` is on, which is off by default because a header is a control. A cell is **editable** only when both the column says so and the table has an `onCellEdit`: the table keeps no copy of the rows, it hands the value over and draws what comes back. `groupBy` gathers rows under headings **after** the search and the sort, with `aggregate` drawing a group's total in the column of the numbers it is a total of, and turns virtual scrolling off. `exportable` writes CSV — every row the search and sort left, not the page — with a byte-order mark, because Excel reads a UTF-8 CSV without one as the local code page.
- [Table](https://neba.cdget.com/components/display/table): A grid of data rendered from a column list and a row list; there are no `<tr>`s to write.
- [List](https://neba.cdget.com/components/display/list): A stack of rows — navigation, settings, results, anything that repeats.
- [Badge](https://neba.cdget.com/components/display/badge): A small mark in the corner of something else: unread mail, a status dot, a count on a tab.
- [Icon](https://neba.cdget.com/components/display/icon): A glyph at a known size, in a known colour. Neba ships no icon set; the glyph is a prop rather than children, and `color` defaults to `inherit`.
- [Image](https://neba.cdget.com/components/display/image): A picture that holds its space while it loads, says when it is loading, and says something useful when it fails — the three things a bare `<img>` leaves to whoever wrote it. `ratio` reserves the box, which is the main reason to use it: an unreserved picture pushes the page down when it lands. A Skeleton stands in while the file arrives and a box carrying the `alt` is drawn if it does not, because the browser's torn-page glyph tells a reader the site is broken rather than that one file is missing. Changing `src` starts both over. `preview` opens the full picture in a Dialog and makes the picture a button named by its alt, so a keyboard reaches it. `alt` is required by the type: a missing one and an empty one mean different things and only the second is ever correct.
- [Blockquote](https://neba.cdget.com/components/display/blockquote): Somebody else's words, set apart from your own. An attribution turns it into the `figure`/`blockquote`/`figcaption` markup the HTML spec asks for.
- [Shortcut](https://neba.cdget.com/components/display/shortcut): A keyboard key or a combination of them. `Mod` resolves to Command on a Mac and Control everywhere else, and every glyph key carries its name for a screen reader.
- [Highlight](https://neba.cdget.com/components/display/highlight): Marks the words a reader is looking for inside text they were already reading. Case, whole words and regular expressions are props; elements in the children are walked into rather than rejected.
- [Timeline](https://neba.cdget.com/components/display/timeline): A sequence of steps in the order they happen. An `<ol>`, because the order is the content; `active` is an index rather than a value, because nothing here is chosen.
- [Gallery](https://neba.cdget.com/components/display/gallery): A set of pictures in one of four arrangements — `grid` gives every tile one shape, `masonry` keeps each picture's proportion and deals it into the shortest column, `justified` keeps the proportions and scales each row to fill the width exactly, and `quilted` lets a tile take more than one cell. Nothing is measured: a tile's shape comes from the item's own `ratio`, so the wall is right in the first frame and does not reflow as the files land. `columns` takes a breakpoint map, `gap` the space between tiles, `caption` puts an item's title and description below the picture or across the foot of it, and `hover` answers the pointer with depth, colour or the one scale the design language allows. `preview` opens the picture full size with the rest of the set an arrow key away, and the viewer is fetched on demand. `filter`, `frame`, `watermark` and `protect` pass through to every tile's Image.
- [AppLogo](https://neba.cdget.com/components/display/app-logo): A product's mark, at a known size, that is never an empty box: an inline SVG, an image, a letter on a tile, or the name itself set as the logotype. `shape` decides the framing — `bare` keeps the artwork's own proportions, `app` and `circle` inset it into a tile — and `showName` draws the words half of a lockup. `href` makes the whole thing the way back to the front page.
- [Avatar](https://neba.cdget.com/components/display/avatar): A picture of a person or a thing, at a known size. Falls back to initials, a glyph or a silhouette when there is no image, so it is never an empty box.
- [Anchor](https://neba.cdget.com/components/display/anchor): The list of headings on the page being read, with the one the reader is in marked. Real `<a href="#…">`s in a real `<nav>`, so they jump whether or not the tracking is running. The marked row is the last heading whose top has passed the line — which reads correctly going up as well as down — and the last heading wins once the scroll reaches the bottom; nothing is marked while the reader is still above the first. `offset` clears a sticky header, `container` names what scrolls when it is not the document, `activeHref` takes the tracking over.
- [DataList](https://neba.cdget.com/components/display/data-list): A list of things and what they are called — a details panel, the metadata under a heading. Real `<dt>`/`<dd>` pairs rather than a two-column Table, because a table is a grid of rows walked as a grid and this is a set of pairs, each read as "label, value". `orientation` puts the label beside the value or above it, `labelWidth` fixes the column so two lists agree, `dividers` scores the rows. It draws no surface.
- [Breadcrumb](https://neba.cdget.com/components/display/breadcrumb): The trail of pages above the one being read. `maxItems` collapses the middle of a long trail, and the last item is the current page rather than a link.
- [TextLink](https://neba.cdget.com/components/display/text-link): A link, in a sentence or on its own. No surface and no height of its own — what it has is the line under it, and a mark for the links that take over the window.
- [TreeView](https://neba.cdget.com/components/display/tree-view): Rows that belong to one another and open and shut — a folder listing, a navigation sidebar, any grouped list a reader needs to fold away. A row can select or can be an `href`.

### Charts

- [Statistic](https://neba.cdget.com/components/charts/statistic): A number with its name on it, and — given a `previousValue` — how far it has moved. `betterWhen` decides which direction is coloured as good.
- [Sparkline](https://neba.cdget.com/components/charts/sparkline): A word-sized picture of a trend, with no axes, no grid and no legend — for beside a number, inside a sentence or in a table cell. `shape` picks a line, an area or bars; it scales itself to its own range unless `min` and `max` say otherwise, which is what makes two of them comparable.
- [LineChart](https://neba.cdget.com/components/charts/line-chart): One or more series against an ordered category axis, for when the space between two points is a journey rather than two separate facts. `curve` is straight, monotone-smooth or stepped; a `null` breaks the line rather than being drawn as a zero; the value axis crops to the data because a line encodes a position.
- [AreaChart](https://neba.cdget.com/components/charts/area-chart): A line with the space under it filled, for a quantity that adds up to something. `stacked` makes the top edge the total and `stacked="full"` normalises every category to 100%, which turns the chart from being about size into being about the mix.
- [BarChart](https://neba.cdget.com/components/charts/bar-chart): Lengths compared across categories. The value axis starts at zero and cannot be talked out of it; `orientation="horizontal"` is the right answer whenever the category names are words; grouped, stacked and 100%-stacked answer three different questions.
- [ScatterChart](https://neba.cdget.com/components/charts/scatter-chart): Two measures per point plotted against each other, for reading whether they move together. Both axes measure, so every point carries an `x` that is a number or a `Date`; a point that also carries a `z` is drawn as a bubble whose *area* is that number, which is what makes a scatter plot and a bubble chart one component. Past three series the marks take a shape each, because the palette only separates three on a plot where any two of them can end up side by side.
- [TimelineChart](https://neba.cdget.com/components/charts/timeline-chart): Rows of spans against a calendar — a Gantt. Each series is a row and each datum a `{ start, end }`, which is its own type rather than a widened `NebaChartPoint`; the axis picks its own unit (seconds through years) and ticks where a calendar ticks rather than on a 1-2-5 step. Not the same component as Timeline, which is a list of steps in `display` and draws no axis.
- [HeatmapChart](https://neba.cdget.com/components/charts/heatmap-chart): A magnitude per cell, coloured rather than measured, in two shapes from one data model — `shape="grid"` for two categorical axes, `shape="treemap"` for squarified tiles sized by share. Colour encodes *size* and so comes off a one-hue sequential ramp (`--neba-chart-seq-*`) or a two-hue diverging one, never the eight-slot categorical palette; the legend is a scale bar with its ends labelled rather than a list of swatches.
- [GaugeChart](https://neba.cdget.com/components/charts/gauge-chart): One number on a scale that is known in advance, drawn as a dial — a Meter bent into an arc, and deliberately the same component in two shapes, so `value`, `min`, `max` and `thresholds` mean exactly what they mean there. `sweep` opens the dial symmetrically about twelve o'clock (180 for a tile, 270 for an instrument, 360 for a ring) and the drawing is sized against the box for the sweep it was given, so a half-dial leaves no empty half above it. Not a PieChart with `shape="semi"`: the unfilled arc is the rest of the dial, not a second category. The reading in the middle is real text.
- [PieChart](https://neba.cdget.com/components/charts/pie-chart): Parts of a whole as slices of a circle, as a pie, a donut or a semicircle. Good for one question — is one of these most of it — and past six slices a BarChart is the honest answer.

Every chart takes the same data: a `series` array (or, for a pie, `data`) of numbers, `null`s that mean a gap rather than a zero, or points carrying their own `x`, `color` and `label`. Colours come from a fixed eight-slot ramp that is never cycled and whose adjacent pairs are verified against simulated protanopia and deuteranopia; a series' slot follows its place in the array, so filtering the legend never repaints the survivors. Every chart also renders its data as a visually hidden table, so no value is reachable only by pointer, and the plot is focusable with the arrow keys stepping the crosshair.

### Feedback

- [Alert](https://neba.cdget.com/components/feedback/alert): A message about something that happened, set into the page it is about.
- [Dialog](https://neba.cdget.com/components/feedback/dialog): A sheet that takes the page away until it is answered.
- [Confirm](https://neba.cdget.com/components/feedback/confirm): "Are you sure?" as something you await. `ConfirmProvider` hosts one Dialog and `useConfirm()` returns a function that resolves to what the reader pressed, so the code that asks is the code that acts — no state per question, no `onConfirm` splitting one decision across two functions. Cancelling, Escape and the backdrop all resolve `false`; it never rejects, because a question answered no is an answer and not a failure. `alert` drops the cancelling button for telling rather than asking, and still resolves. Questions queue rather than replacing each other: resolving an older one to make room would report an answer nobody gave, which at the call site reads as "they said no".
- [Popconfirm](https://neba.cdget.com/components/feedback/popconfirm): The same question asked beside the control that raised it rather than over the page. The choice between the two is **reach**, not danger or size: the consequence is this row, this file, this tag — Popconfirm; the consequence goes past what is on screen — Confirm. The bubble closes when `onConfirm` *settles*, so an async handler keeps it up with its button busy. `onCancel` fires for the cancelling button and not for Escape or a click outside, because walking away from a question is not the same act as answering no. `color` defaults to `danger` and `icon` draws that family's severity mark, which is shape carrying meaning rather than decoration.
- [Toast](https://neba.cdget.com/components/feedback/toast): A message that arrives on its own, over whatever is already on the page.
- [Tooltip](https://neba.cdget.com/components/feedback/tooltip): A short label that appears when the pointer rests on something.
- [ProgressLinear](https://neba.cdget.com/components/feedback/progress-linear): A bar that fills. The workhorse of the three progress indicators.
- [ProgressCircular](https://neba.cdget.com/components/feedback/progress-circular): A ring that fills, for where there is no room for a bar.
- [ProgressBox](https://neba.cdget.com/components/feedback/progress-box): A row of acrylic plates that light up.
- [Overlay](https://neba.cdget.com/components/feedback/overlay): A sheet over the whole page that stops it being used — the scrim on its own.
- [Skeleton](https://neba.cdget.com/components/feedback/skeleton): The shape of something that has not loaded yet, in a line, a block or a circle. It reserves the space the real thing will take, so nothing on the page moves when the content arrives.
- [Tour](https://neba.cdget.com/components/feedback/tour): A guided walk over a page that already exists — the three things a new reader has to be shown once, pointed at where they actually are. HowToSteps turned inside out: that one puts the instructions in the page, this one leaves the page alone and stands over it, so each step names its target with a CSS selector rather than restating it. The dimming is one element with a hole in it and never takes the pointer, so the control being pointed at stays usable — which is the difference between a tour and a sequence of dialogs. A step with no `target` is centred, for a welcome or a closing card.
- [Meter](https://neba.cdget.com/components/feedback/meter): How much of something there is on a scale that is known in advance — disk used, seats taken, quota spent. The same groove a ProgressLinear cuts and not the same component: `value` is required, because a meter reports a quantity that is already known rather than something in flight. `thresholds` is the reason it exists — a list of `{ from, color }` points, so the semantic family follows the reading instead of being a ternary at every call site.
- [Empty](https://neba.cdget.com/components/feedback/empty): What stands where content would have been — a glyph, a headline, a sentence and an `action`. The headline defaults to the `locale`'s way of saying there is nothing here, and `variant` defaults to `text` because an empty state is usually already inside a Card or a Table. The other half of Skeleton: one is content on its way, the other is content that is not coming.

### Layout

- [PageLayout](https://neba.cdget.com/components/layout/page-layout): The skeleton a page is hung on — a header, a footer, one sidebar or two, and the content between them, each in a real landmark. `headerSpan` decides whether the bar or the rails take the top corner, `scroll` whether the document or only the content scrolls, and `collapseBelow` the width at which the sidebars become drawers. It draws no surface and no gutter; put a Container inside.
- [Header](https://neba.cdget.com/components/layout/header): The bar across the top of a page, divided into a leading `brand` slot, a middle and a trailing `actions` slot. A real `<header>`, so the banner landmark. `align="center"` puts the middle on the bar's own midline by giving both ends an equal share.
- [Footer](https://neba.cdget.com/components/layout/footer): The sheet at the end of a page — a real `<footer>`, the contentinfo landmark. It has no slots on purpose: it decides the surface, the gutter, the hairline that says the document ended, and whether the bar stays in reach; the content is the caller's.
- [Sidebar](https://neba.cdget.com/components/layout/sidebar): A column beside the page's content, and a Drawer once the window is narrower than `collapseBelow` — one component, and the children exist once either way. A real `<aside>`. `resizable` lets the inner edge be dragged, `side` is logical so it flips under RTL, and SidebarTrigger is the button that brings it back.
- [Container](https://neba.cdget.com/components/layout/container): Horizontal breathing room around whatever it wraps; keeps a page's content off the edge of the window. `maxWidth` is the optional measure: a step of the ladder (`xs` 30rem through `xl` 80rem, the upper four being the breakpoint floors), any CSS length of your own, or a per-breakpoint map. Header and Footer take the same prop in the same shape.
- [Grid](https://neba.cdget.com/components/layout/grid): A responsive layout on twelve columns. Every grid is wrapped in a GridContainer and each cell is a Grid.
- [Panes](https://neba.cdget.com/components/layout/panes): A box divided into regions with a draggable bar between each pair — an editor beside a file list, a preview beside a form. Panes nest, and a Pane can opt out of being resizable.
- [ScrollArea](https://neba.cdget.com/components/layout/scroll-area): A box with a scrollbar of its own, because the browser's is drawn by the operating system — a different width on every machine and a different colour from the sheet it is cut into. `orientation` is one axis or both, `height`/`maxHeight` is what bounds it, and `fade` dims the content at each edge that has more beyond it and only there, drawn as a mask so it works over a translucent surface. Not ScrollZone, which is a rail with stepper buttons.
- [ScrollZone](https://neba.cdget.com/components/layout/scroll-zone): A strip of anything laid out in one direction and scrolled in it — a row of cards, a rail of chips, a column of rows. `lines` fills two or more rows before starting a new column, so one scroll holds twice as much; `mode` decides what a scroll button does (one item, one page, or continuously while held) and `buttons` whether they are drawn at all. It is an ordinary scroll container underneath, so touch, the scrollbar and the arrow keys are the browser's own; `drag` adds the same pull for a mouse, and `wheel` turns a wheel rolled over the strip into travel along it, handing it back to the page at either end.
- [Stack](https://neba.cdget.com/components/layout/stack): Things laid over each other, so a set reads as a pile rather than a row. `direction` is `horizontal`, `vertical` or `diagonal` (a fanned deck); `overlap` and `drop` are how far each item sits under the last. `max`/`total`/`overflow` turn the ones that did not fit into one more item at the back. `scaleStep` and `opacityStep` make the pile recede, `front` says which end is on top, and `transition` with `stagger` deals it one item at a time. The overlap is a margin, not a translate, so the box is exactly as big as what is in it.
- [Flex](https://neba.cdget.com/components/layout/flex): A row, or a column, and the width at which it changes from one to the other. `direction` is `horizontal`/`vertical` and is responsive, which is the prop it exists for; `spacing`, `rowSpacing` and `columnSpacing` are the gutter on the same scale and through the same slot a GridContainer uses, the axis ones laid over `spacing` rather than replacing it. `wrap` is off by default, the opposite of a grid. It draws nothing — no surface, no padding, no gutter unless asked.
- [Show](https://neba.cdget.com/components/layout/show): Its children at some widths and not at others. `above` is an inclusive floor and `below` an exclusive ceiling on the five breakpoints, so the same name in both covers every width exactly once. The children are always rendered and what changes is `display`, which is what makes the answer right in the first painted frame and the same on a server; `useBreakpoint` is for the decision CSS cannot make, which is not rendering something at all. The wrapper is `display: contents`, so it adds no box.
- [AspectRatio](https://neba.cdget.com/components/layout/aspect-ratio): A box that keeps a proportion whatever width it is given. `ratio` is CSS's own `aspect-ratio`, and `fit` stretches a single piece of media to the box and fits it.
- [Portal](https://neba.cdget.com/components/layout/portal): Children rendered somewhere else in the DOM, usually the end of `<body>`, for a subtree that has to escape a clipping or stacking context. Two things it adds over `createPortal`: the wrapper carries `neba-portal`, the class this library's own popups use and a scoped stylesheet hangs its reset off — a portalled subtree leaves whatever element the page scoped its styling to, and the class is how it is found again; and it renders nothing at all until it has mounted, because there is no `document` on a server. `container` takes an element or a function called after mount; `disabled` renders in place, and has to be decided once, since flipping it remounts everything inside. It is placement and nothing else — no focus trap, no Escape, no click-outside.

### Surfaces

- [Box](https://neba.cdget.com/components/surfaces/box): A sheet of acrylic with content on it. The plainest surface in the library.
- [Card](https://neba.cdget.com/components/surfaces/card): A Box with the parts a card is made of — title, subtitle, body, footer. Every Box prop passes through.
- [Accordion](https://neba.cdget.com/components/surfaces/accordion): A stack of sections that fold. Opening one closes the last.
- [Tabs](https://neba.cdget.com/components/surfaces/tabs): One set of panels, one of which is shown. Horizontal or vertical.
- [Carousel](https://neba.cdget.com/components/surfaces/carousel): A strip of slides, one of which is in view. A scroll-snap container, so it swipes, runs the other way under RTL, and transforms nothing.
- [Pill](https://neba.cdget.com/components/surfaces/pill): A floating lozenge holding a small amount of live information, optionally growing into a second half. The one fully round shape in the library.
- [Toolbar](https://neba.cdget.com/components/surfaces/toolbar): A bar of controls — an application header, a page's action row. `start`, `children` and `end` are the three slots; `position` pins it.
- [ChatBubble](https://neba.cdget.com/components/surfaces/chat-bubble): One message in a conversation. The avatar, the sender, the time, the delivery mark, the media above the text and the link card below it are each drawn only when they are given something.
- [Drawer](https://neba.cdget.com/components/surfaces/drawer): A panel attached to one edge of the window. `mode="overlay"` floats it over the page on a scrim; `mode="inline"` puts the same panel in the layout as a fixed sidebar. The corners on the free edge are cut and the ones against the window stay square.
- [HoverCard](https://neba.cdget.com/components/surfaces/hover-card): A card that opens when the pointer rests on something and holds a preview of what is on the other side of it. It sits between the other two popups: a Tooltip is a label the pointer never reaches, a Popover was asked for by a press. This one is uninvited like the first and reachable like the second, so a link inside it can be followed. `delay` and `closeDelay` decide how long it waits and how long it stays — the second is what makes the gap between the trigger and the card crossable. Whatever is in it must also exist on the page the trigger leads to, because a keyboard, a touchscreen and a screen reader all arrive by that route instead.
- [Popover](https://neba.cdget.com/components/surfaces/popover): A sheet that opens beside the control that opened it. Unlike a Tooltip it stays up and can be reached, so a form, a filter panel or a picker belongs in it; unlike a Dialog it does not take the page.
- [Mockup](https://neba.cdget.com/components/surfaces/mockup): A device with a screen you can put anything on — a phone, a tablet, a monitor or a laptop, with the system's own status bar, dock or taskbar drawn on it. `device` picks the machine, `os` the chrome, `bezel` and `finish` the hardware, `notch` the camera cut-out. The screen is a viewport at the device's real resolution and a container named `neba-screen`, so content inside lays out against the device rather than the page.
- [WindowPane](https://neba.cdget.com/components/surfaces/window-pane): Anything at all, drawn the way one of four systems draws a window — `os` is one of eight — `macos`, `macosx` (Aqua), `windows11`, `windows10`, `windows8`, `windows7` (Aero), `windowsxp` (Luna) and `linux` — a version being its own entry wherever the title bar is what changed, and it decides where the controls sit, how they are drawn, what colour the bar is, how thick the frame is and how the corners are cut. It is a frame that behaves rather than a picture of one: `draggable` moves it on `left`/`top` (never a transform), `resizable` puts handles on every edge and corner, and `controls` are real buttons wired to controlled/uncontrolled `open`, `minimized` and `maximized`. `accent` dyes the title bar, `transparency` lets the page through the chrome and turns the acrylic on with it.
- [HowToSteps](https://neba.cdget.com/components/surfaces/how-to-steps): A guide the reader walks through — numbered steps down one side, one step's instructions beside them, and a way forward under those. `steps` is an array of `{ title, content?, image? }`; `orientation` runs the numbers down a column or across the top; `maxHeight` scrolls a long list and keeps the current row in view; `divider` draws a hairline between the list and the body; `transition` is the entrance a step arrives with, from the library's usual motion vocabulary, with `'none'` to turn it off. A step's `icon` is drawn before its title over the body and never in the list, where the numbered disc already says which step it is. Every step's body is rendered into the same grid cell, so the panel keeps the height of the tallest and the card does not resize as the reader moves. It is Timeline's interactive sibling: a Timeline reports, a HowToSteps asks.
- [Spoiler](https://neba.cdget.com/components/surfaces/spoiler): Content that stays covered until somebody asks for it. The cover is a blur rather than a hidden box, so a reader can see that there is something there and how much of it.
- [Collapsible](https://neba.cdget.com/components/surfaces/collapsible): One section that folds, standing on its own — what an Accordion is a set of. `title`, `subtitle`, `startIcon` and `action` build the header, `trigger` replaces it with a control of your own, and `hiddenUntilFound` lets the browser's page search open it.

### Transitions

Wrappers that make anything move. Every one takes the same settings — `duration` and `delay` in milliseconds, `easing`, `repeat` (a count or `'infinite'`), `alternate`, `paused`, and `trigger` (`'mount'`, `'visible'`, `'hover'` or `'manual'` with `play`). All of them are switched off entirely by a `prefers-reduced-motion` preference, so none of them is ever the only thing carrying a message. The six named effects are also available as a `transition` prop on the components that display something — Box, Card, Statistic, Alert, Chip, Avatar, Icon, Typography, Blockquote — where they run once on mount; they are offered on no component that is pressed.

- [AnimateFade](https://neba.cdget.com/components/transitions/animate-fade): Content arriving or leaving on opacity alone. Nothing moves, so nothing reflows and no text is resampled. `mode="out"` is the same animation reversed and held at the end.
- [AnimateGrow](https://neba.cdget.com/components/transitions/animate-grow): Content unfolding from a point. `origin` anchors it to any edge or corner, so it reads as opening out of the thing beside it.
- [AnimateZoom](https://neba.cdget.com/components/transitions/animate-zoom): The same arithmetic as Grow at more than twice the distance and always about the centre — for the one thing on a screen meant to interrupt.
- [AnimateSlide](https://neba.cdget.com/components/transitions/animate-slide): Content travelling in from one edge. The default distance is the element's own size, so it starts exactly out of frame.
- [AnimateRotate](https://neba.cdget.com/components/transitions/animate-rotate): Content turning about a point. Two angles rather than one, so it covers both a glyph swinging into place and an endless spin.
- [AnimateBlink](https://neba.cdget.com/components/transitions/animate-blink): Content pulsing to a floor and back. Symmetric, so however many times it runs it ends where it started.
- [AnimateAppear](https://neba.cdget.com/components/transitions/animate-appear): A list settling into place one child after another. The animation is written onto the children themselves, so a list stays the shape it was.
- [AnimateReveal](https://neba.cdget.com/components/transitions/animate-reveal): Content uncovered by an edge travelling across it — nothing moves and nothing changes colour. `side` is the edge the wipe comes from, `from` fades as it wipes, `mode="out"` covers it up again. It is a `clip-path`, so there is no wrapper and the element takes exactly the room it always took.
- [AnimateFloat](https://neba.cdget.com/components/transitions/animate-float): A slow drift with nowhere to get to, for something that is not fixed to the page. `from` and `distance` say which way and how far; it repeats forever and turns round at both ends. Never on a control.
- [AnimateShake](https://neba.cdget.com/components/transitions/animate-shake): The one effect that says no — a wrong password, a form that would not send. Defaults to `trigger="manual"`; bind `play` to the failure and give it a fresh `key` on each one. Never give it a `repeat`.
- [AnimateSplit](https://neba.cdget.com/components/transitions/animate-split): A line of text arriving a word — or, with `by="character"`, a letter — at a time. `effect` picks which animation each piece uses and `stagger` is what the effect is made of. The whole line stays in the document once for a screen reader.
- [AnimateCounter](https://neba.cdget.com/components/transitions/animate-counter): A number counted up to its `value`. `format` is `Intl.NumberFormat` options, so a currency or a compact `1.2M` is a prop. Pairs with `Statistic`, whose `value` takes a node. `trigger="visible"` for a dashboard below the fold.
- [AnimateScramble](https://neba.cdget.com/components/transitions/animate-scramble): Text resolving out of noise one character at a time, in a box that is the finished length from the first frame — so nothing around it reflows. Whitespace is never scrambled.
- [AnimateTyping](https://neba.cdget.com/components/transitions/animate-typing): Text typed one character at a time, counted in graphemes. The whole string is in the document from the first frame for a screen reader; the animated copy is `aria-hidden`.
- [AnimateLighting](https://neba.cdget.com/components/transitions/animate-lighting): A light travelling around the outside of something, behind the content rather than on it — so it marks what it wraps without altering how that is drawn.
- [AnimateMarquee](https://neba.cdget.com/components/transitions/animate-marquee): Content scrolling steadily past, laid down twice so there is no seam. `speed` is pixels per second rather than a duration, and it stops under the pointer.
- [AnimateHeadline](https://neba.cdget.com/components/transitions/animate-headline): One line replacing the one above it on a timer. Every line shares a grid cell, so the box never resizes as the reel turns.

## Examples

- [Overview](https://neba.cdget.com/examples/overview): Every component in the library on a single product-shaped screen, with a block-by-block breakdown of which components each part uses.
- [Landing page](https://neba.cdget.com/examples/concept-landing): A marketing page built only from these components — mostly type, space and one call to action repeated.
- [Admin dashboard](https://neba.cdget.com/examples/concept-dashboard): A nav rail, a filter row, four figures, a table with an action on every row and a drawer of settings, all at the same size.
- [Sign-up page](https://neba.cdget.com/examples/concept-signup): Registration in three steps — every kind of answer a form can ask for, and the states around them.
